newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks take another dive on economy woes.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks take another dive on economy woes.

text.p: Japanese stocks took another steep tumble on Wednesday, with the key market index falling 1.14 percent to its lowest close in more than a year on deepening gloom about the domestic economy.
Growing worries over construction firms and financial institutions, already suffering from bad loan problems, overshadowed the market, brokers said.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 average shed 215.81 points or 1.14 percent to close at 18,680.38, its lowest close since November 29, 1995, when the index ended at 18,533.98.
On Tuesday, the Nikkei had plunged almost 550 points to close at 18,896.19.
"Unless shares in the (financial and building) sectors stop sliding, overall sentiment will not recover," said Michio Sugita, head of stock trading at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
